people.name: Lee Zeldin
people.role: Administrator, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency
people.position: EPA under Zeldin issued a May 2025 memorandum limiting states' and tribes' use of Clean Water Act Section 401 to water-quality purposes and proposed revised Section 401 rules in January 2026, framing the limits as supporting energy, minerals and infrastructure projects. Stance is toward permitting reform generally; EPA has not commented on the Sept. 30, 2026 bill in sources reviewed.
key_actions: 2025-05-22: EPA issued a memorandum on the limited role of states and tribes under Clean Water Act Section 401
2026-01-15: EPA's proposed rule updating the Section 401 water quality certification regulations was published

quote.text: With this memorandum, EPA is reinforcing the limits on Clean Water Act section 401 certification to support energy, critical mineral, and infrastructure projects

sources.title: EPA Reinforces Alignment of Clean Water Act Section 401 with 'Powering the Great American Comeback' Initiative
Updating the Water Quality Certification Regulations (proposed rule, 91 FR 2008)

people.name: Ross Marchand
people.role: Executive Director, Taxpayers Protection Alliance
people.position: TPA welcomed the Sept. 30, 2026 bill's review deadlines, litigation limits and regulatory certainty but urged lawmakers to improve and clarify its provisions requiring data centers to cover their transmission costs, which it says should follow transparent, technology-neutral cost allocation.
key_actions: 2026-09-30: Issued TPA's statement welcoming the bipartisan permitting deal while criticizing the data-center cost provisions

quote.text: America desperately needs permitting reform, and this bipartisan proposal contains plenty of promising ideas for taxpayers and consumers to welcome.

sources.title: Taxpayer Watchdog Welcomes Bipartisan Permitting Deal

people.name: Brent Gardner
people.role: Chief Government Affairs Officer, Americans for Prosperity
people.position: AFP celebrated House passage of the SPEED Act as the most significant NEPA reform in more than 50 years and urged the Senate to take it up. Stance shown is toward the House bill and permitting reform generally; no AFP statement on the Sept. 30, 2026 Senate bill was found.
key_actions: 2025-12-18: Issued AFP's statement celebrating House passage of the SPEED Act 221-196

quote.text: America wants to build and for too long, Washington bureaucrats have said no.

sources.title: Americans for Prosperity Celebrates Bipartisan Passage of the SPEED Act in the House

people.name: Brett Hartl
people.role: Government Affairs Director, Center for Biological Diversity
people.position: Opposes the Sept. 30, 2026 bill, arguing it would dismantle Endangered Species Act and Clean Water Act protections and give the fossil fuel industry long-term advantages in exchange for minimal gains for renewables and transmission.
key_actions: 2026-09-30: Issued the Center's statement calling the bill a 'climate kill shot'

quote.text: This is a climate kill shot that condemns our most vulnerable communities to suffer decades more fossil fuel pollution.

sources.title: Democrats Abandon Environmental Laws to Advance Pro-Fossil Fuel 'Permitting Reform'

people.name: Jim Walsh
people.role: Policy Director, Food & Water Watch
people.position: Opposes the Sept. 30, 2026 bill, calling it a power grab by Big Tech and the fossil fuel industry to fast-track data centers that limits states' ability to protect water resources, and criticizing Senate Democrats for relying on administration promises on wind and solar.
key_actions: 2026-09-30: Issued Food & Water Watch's statement opposing the bipartisan permitting plan

quote.text: This bill is a power grab by Big Tech and the fossil fuel industry to fast-track AI data centers and their egregious thirst for energy and water, while limiting the ability of states to protect water resources.

sources.title: Bipartisan Permitting Reform Plan is Danger to Public Health, Enviro Protection, States' Rights

people.name: Joe Manchin
people.role: Former U.S. Senator and former Chairman, Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee
people.position: Background figure: co-wrote the 2024 Energy Permitting Reform Act with John Barrasso, which cleared the Senate Energy Committee 15-4 but never reached a floor vote. He is no longer in office, and no statement from him on the Sept. 30, 2026 bill was found.
key_actions: 2024-07-22: Released the Energy Permitting Reform Act draft with Sen. Barrasso
2024-07-31: The Senate ENR Committee advanced S. 4753 by a 15-4 vote

quote.text: meaningful and reasonable changes when it comes to both energy production and emissions reductions

sources.title: Energy Chairman Manchin's Permitting Bill Moves Through Committee in Careful Balancing Act
Senate Energy & Natural Resources Committee Passes Permitting Bill

people.name: Brett Kavanaugh
people.role: Associate Justice, Supreme Court of the United States
people.affiliation: Supreme Court of the United States
people.position: Wrote the Court's opinion in Seven County Infrastructure Coalition v. Eagle County, directing courts to give agencies substantial deference on NEPA reviews; lower courts have since applied it, including the D.C. Circuit in July 2026. No position on the Sept. 30, 2026 bill applies.
key_actions: 2025-05-29: Authored the Court's opinion in Seven County, reversing the D.C. Circuit's vacatur of the Uinta Basin Railway approval

quote.text: Simply stated, NEPA is a procedural cross-check, not a substantive roadblock. The goal of the law is to inform agency decisionmaking, not to paralyze it.

people.name: Josh Siegel
people.role: Energy reporter, E&E News by POLITICO
people.position: Reporter covering the Senate permitting talks. In August 2026 he reported that negotiators had missed an early-August deal and were eyeing September, and on the morning of Sept. 30 he reported that a senior Democratic aide said the deal was on hold over changed offshore wind language hours before the text was released.
key_actions: 2026-08-07: Reported that Senate negotiators and lobbyists were eyeing September as a new deadline after failing to reach a deal that week
2026-09-30: Reported on X that a senior Democratic aide said the permitting deal was on hold after staff found offshore wind language had changed; the bill was released the same day
